scope: Read-only source review for explicit --native-dense-gguf controls and external --ple-gguf placement. No runtime or model was launched.

findings.finding: --ple-gguf assigns one path; --native-dense-gguf appends each repeated argument to a vector.
--native expands the original split shards; without --ple-gguf, GgufModel finds per_layer_token_embd.weight and selects its containing shard.

Only when native_dense_gguf is empty, it defaults to native_shards and appends a non-strata-ple PLE path unless that exact path string is already present. An E-copy path differs from F shard 2, so defaulting would append it.

NativeDense eligibility is a dense projection suffix allowlist plus optional blk.1.ple_key.weight; per_layer_token_embd.weight is not a native-dense tensor. served_names collects served names for pack skipping.
A repeated eligible tensor name during native dense loading is an error, not silently deduplicated.
Duplicate tensor names inside one GGUF file are rejected on open.
The PLE table is opened separately from o.ple_gguf. With an explicit shared native-dense list, only this PLE table source path varies between arms.
weight_bytes_for uses a seen tensor-name set and skips duplicates for sizing; its source comment explicitly says load refuses them.
The sizing helper is called before native dense loading, so its duplicate-name skip is not proof the later NativeDense::load accepts duplicate shards.
Actual load validates unique split.no and rejects duplicate eligible tensor names; runtime does not silently de-duplicate repeated source paths.
The PLE row table key per_layer_token_embd.weight is outside NativeDense eligible names; optional blk.1.ple_key.weight is a distinct tensor from the PLE table.

conclusion.only_intended_placement_contrast: --ple-gguf original F shard 2 vs byte-identical E shard 2 copy
conclusion.default_list_risk: The default native-dense list starts as four F model shards. A distinct external E shard-2 path is appended unless metadata identifies a standalone strata-ple file; the E copy is byte-identical to the original Qwen shard-2 model file. The paired F2/E2 split.no values therefore collide in NativeDense::load. weight_bytes_for may skip duplicate names while sizing, but that does not prevent the later load error.
conclusion.same_file_F_arm_note: F shard 2 appears once in the shared native-dense list and as the F PLE reader path. per_layer_token_embd.weight is not NativeDense eligible, so the table itself is read by the separate PLE reader rather than uploaded a second time as a dense tensor.
conclusion.duplicate_handling: The parser appends repeated native-dense arguments. The exact-string std::find avoids only a path string already in the vector; no canonical-file identity de-dup is performed. Runtime load rejects duplicate split numbers and duplicate eligible tensor names. GGUF parsing rejects duplicate names within a single file.
